tagline: The birthplace of bibimbap is Korea's food capital, with more than 700 traditional hanok houses in Jeonju Hanok Village and a UNESCO City of Gastronomy title.
overview: Jeonju, the capital of North Jeolla Province, is the spiritual home of the Joseon dynasty: the royal Yi family came from here, and Gyeonggijeon shrine holds a portrait of the dynasty's founder, King Taejo. It has been named a UNESCO Creative City of Gastronomy.

Jeonju Hanok Village is the city's highlight, with more than 700 traditional tiled-roof houses, many now guesthouses, cafés and craft workshops. Visitors stroll in rented hanbok past Jeondong Cathedral, Gyeonggijeon and the Omokdae hill viewpoint.

Food is the main reason many people come. Jeonju bibimbap, served in a brass bowl with many toppings, is famous across Korea, as are kongnamul gukbap (bean sprout soup) and makgeolli houses where every round brings more dishes. The Jeonju International Film Festival fills the city every spring.
